main_text.p: tio lib.15.Epist.13.in qua cur de officiis libros filio infcripferit,oftédit lib.16.Epist.6.in qua libri de gloria meminit: & 11. eiufdem in qua infcriptionis officiorum caufas reddit.Imitationis exemplum.Nos exercitij gratia 8.lib.9. famil. imitari conabimur, in qua libros fuos Academicos Varroni Cicero mittit, eundemq; monet,vt de Latina lingua inchoatos libros abfoluere & ad fe mittere velit.Partes funt quatuor: quarum prima caufarum expofitionem cotinet,cur Academicos ad Varronem libros mittat. Altera methodi inftitutæ, & perfonarum, quibus fermo in dialogo tribuitur,rationes complectitur.Tertia [illegible, ~8 letters] partim cohortatione ad excolenda ftudia, & vel fimilia vel alia tractanda: partim pollicitatione aliorum fcriptorum conftat. Postrema [illegible, ~6 letters] voto abfoluitur: vt bene feliciterq; emptio &migratio eueniat.Haf-ce ergo fecuti partes orationes à nobis confectas amico mittemus,eundemq; vt pari par referat hortabimur hoc modo.

I. Etsi munus postulare, quamuis quis promife-rit,hominis parum prudentis atq; verecundi esse videatur,tamen scriptorum tuorũ desiderio moueor,amicos tibi hosce vt mittam,qui te non flagitent: sed moneant ac rogent,vt promissis te exoluas atq; liberes.

page.notes: Greek words in the first paragraph (after "Tertia" and "Postrema") are not legible enough to transcribe with confidence; they are marked illegible. The page opens with a fragment ("tio"). The word "amicos" and "videatur" are joined across line ends without a printed hyphen. The marginal note is set in italic type. The Greek word after "Tertia" appears to be a Greek adjective, probably "θεωρητική". The Greek after "Postrema" appears to be "εὐχῇ", but this is not certain.
